text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- Some 30 percent of the 3.47 million cars registred in Romania are concentrated in Bucharest and four counties.
- Romanian Oil Company plans to restructure and put an end to the monopoly in refining, transport and distribution of oil products.
- Romanian annual consumption of scotch whisky is estimated at 1.3 million litres, of which 98 percent is smuggled in.
- Romanian will export 900,000 cubic metres of timber in 1997.
ADEVARUL

- U.S. helicopter maker Bell Helicopter Textron has acquired 70 percent of local plane maker IAR Brasov and will manufacture a variation of its Cobra attack helicopters there. The first 96 helicopters will be purchased by the Romanian military.
- The central bank sees reserves up at $2 billion in June, after it bought $800 million from the market starting February, governor Mugur Isarescu said.
- Shell Oil Products is interested in expanding its distribution network in Romania by means of participating in the country's privatisation process.
- Romania will remove value added tax for tourism firms.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Senate's economic commission has rejected a list of 75 farms to be liquidated in 1997, saying many of them are able to recover.
- Central bank governor Isarescu expects many Romanian companies to issue bonds on international markets in the second half of 1997.
- Bucharest hosts an international consumer goods fair starting May 22. Some 430 foreign companies are exhibiting.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will address the press on May 27 to present the first six months of his goverment's activity.
- The government is planning a bill to allow four percent tax on profits derived from portfolio investments, to lure foreign investors into Romania's capital market.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The Senate's economic commission rejected a recent road tax saying it increased taxation.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Netherlands will support Romania in its bid to join NATO in the first wave, Ciorbea said upon arrival from a brief visit to the Hague.
- President Emil Constantinescu starts a visit to Athens on Thursday to persuade Greece that Romania's NATO membership is not a danger to Russia, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL
- Some 30 Romanians were arrested in France for carrying forged Spanish passports.
- The government decided to cut 27,000 jobs in the medical sector.
- Romania has come a long way on its road to win early NATO admission, the newspaper says quoting a series of articles in U.S. newspapers.
- Hungarian President Arpad Goncz on Sunday starts a three-day visit to Romania to sign accords on tourism and environmental protection.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- The costs of NATO integration for Hungary, Poland, the Czech Republic, Romania and Slovenia are currently evaluated at $5 billion by the U.S. administration, down from a previous estimate of up to $35 billion, the newspaper says.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
